A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MathTutorBench and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original tutoring-model evaluations, reward-model comparisons and ablations, classifier results, and qualitative scoring examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds reward-model runtime and throughput measurements in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The reward-model architecture, pairwise ranking loss, preference-pair construction, and criteria-based scoring remain unchanged. Explicit MRBench label values and the clarification about unavailable margins add documentation without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven math-tutoring tasks, benchmark datasets, normal and hard dialogue scenarios, and reward-model training and testing sources. The dataset statistics match after relocating v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 2.

E2.justification: The eight benchmark models and all judge, reward-model, and classifier comparators are retained. Comparator membership matches between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 4, and between v1 Figure 3 and v2 Figure 4.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the reported test exclusion criterion from overlapping instances/problems to overlapping topics, while retaining 482 examples; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Appendix C.2 also introduces timing on a GH200 GPU at batch sizes 1 and 8.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a small efficiency analysis comparing throughput at two batch sizes. The existing training-data ablations, reward-distribution analysis, classifier checks, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added runtime measurements also contain no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, ablation results, plotted results, and appendix qualitative scores are unchanged. New Appendix C.2 reports scoring 2,954 generations in under 10 minutes on one GH200, with throughput of 7.01 examples/second at batch size 1 and 7.25 at batch size 8.

T1.justification: The mathematical task definitions, ranking loss, preference-score construction, and pairwise accuracy formula remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims: automatic tutoring evaluation, a pedagogical reward model, the expertise–pedagogy trade-off, and difficulties with longer dialogues.

C2.justification: The interpretations and substantive limitations remain the same. The added phrase contrasting general human preferences with pedagogical preferences repeats an explanation already present in v1 Section 6.2.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the desired MRBench category values, identifies TRL alongside Transformers, and documents inference hardware and batching performance. Existing training hyperparameters, checkpoint identifiers, and benchmark prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references to Graesser et al., Litman and Forbes-Riley, Boyer et al., the Qwen2.5 technical report, and TRL. Research positioning remains stable; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording corrections, an expanded Section 5.2, moving training-data documentation into the main text, and revising Appendix C. Affiliations, acknowledgements, and bibliography entries are also updated; most prose and the overall structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The preference-data table moves from the appendix to the main text, the benchmark table moves nearer the results, and several displays are reordered. Figures 3 and 4 exchange numbering, and Figure 5 changes from colored backgrounds to white. Existing plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit preference-label mappings and library details improve reproducibility, while the new runtime measurements substantiate the benchmark's practical scoring cost. The scientific results remain unchanged. The stronger topic-exclusion statement lacks operational detail, so it does not establish improved validation; the overall gains are limited.
